title: AI hardware stocks have been bleeding since July, but looking at actual Q3 numbers and token curves, demand isn't going anywhere
author: ChinaChipChat_
selftext:
People have been panicking over AI hardware stocks sliding since all the way back in July, with everyone assuming demand is finally hitting a wall. But if you actually stack up the Q3 financial reports, big tech capex guides, and monthly token traffic together, the whole narrative about cooling demand doesn't really hold up.

![img](y6d84ebdx41i1 "Ran into formatting issues trying to translate the table, so here's the raw chart (sorry!).")

Looking at the Q3 revenue numbers across the supply chain, growth hasn't slowed down at all. AI compute chips shot up 102 percent year-over-year and actually accelerated to 25 percent quarter-over-quarter, beating Q2's 21 percent. PCBs pulled similar numbers at 52 percent YoY and 22 percent QoQ, while memory went parabolic with a 375 percent YoY surge driven by tight supply and higher prices. Optical modules grew 105 percent YoY and 17 percent QoQ, or 22 percent if you adjust for the roughly 2.1 billion RMB of shipments that got stuck due to the late September floods in Thailand. Meanwhile, OSAT packaging lines are still running at absolute full capacity.

Big tech spending plans back this up on the macro side. Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta all kept or raised their 2026 capex floors, combining for well over 700 billion dollars and making it clear that heavy infrastructure spending is locked in right through 2027. Microsoft only trimmed its guide slightly from 175 billion to 170 billion dollars because third-party compute deliveries got pushed back rather than any drop in Azure demand, and their Q4 spending is bouncing right back over 50 billion dollars.

Downstream usage tells the exact same story from the demand side. Monthly token volume on OpenRouter scaled roughly 22.5 times from January to October to an estimated 720 trillion tokens. Agent workflows overtook simple human chat traffic way back in February and are now pulling seven times more volume, with nearly 90 percent of those agent tokens leveraging prompt caching to cut repeat context costs and handle much longer tasks.

The recent market selloff looks a lot more like Wall Street just digesting extreme valuations, high interest rates, and temporary hardware supply bottlenecks than any actual collapse in real AI demand.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: both can be true. the stocks paid for this growth a year ago, so a strong Q3 only confirms what was already in the price. what multiples are the names you follow on now versus July?
